questions.q: How many wings did Jibril have when the Prophet SAW saw him in his true form?
questions.explain: Jibril appeared with six hundred wings, and the Prophet fell and ran home.

questions.q: Who read the Gospel and the Torah, recognised An-Namus and died a few days later?
questions.explain: Waraqah was Khadijah's elderly, blind cousin.

questions.q: What did Allah command in Surah Al-Muzzammil?
questions.explain: Allah told him to stand for the night prayer.

questions.q: How did the Prophet SAW feel when the revelation was cut off?
questions.explain: He was restless and sad when the revelation paused for a while.

questions.q: Which surah did Jibril bring to comfort him after the revelation was cut off?
questions.explain: Jibril came again with Surah Ad-Duha, which calmed him.

options: Morning when the sun rises gently
questions.explain: Ad-Duha is the morning when the sun rises softly and is not yet scorching.

questions.q: Who was the first friend to believe and then brought his own friends to Islam?
questions.explain: Abu Bakr bravely followed when others were afraid.

questions.q: What did Allah remind him of about his early life?
options: You were raised in a palace
Did He not find you an orphan and shelter you
questions.explain: Allah reminded him of past favours: an orphan who was sheltered, one searching who was guided.

questions.q: Allah abandoned and hated the Prophet SAW when the revelation was cut off.
questions.explain: False. Allah does not abandon or hate His servant even when we are sad.

questions.q: The Prophet SAW preached quietly for three years, from age 40 to 43.
questions.explain: True. After that the call became public.

questions.q: You meet a sad orphan. What should you do?
options: Look after and comfort them kindly
questions.explain: Orphans need to be cared for and comforted, not scolded or troubled.

questions.q: Match each term with its meaning.

right.text: The pause when revelation stopped for a while

questions.explain: Al-Muzzammil is the one wrapped in garments, the pause is a break in revelation, huda is guidance and aghna means to make sufficient.
